text_en: And Judith said, Begin a song to my God with tambourines, sing to my Lord with cymbals. Raise to him a new psalm; exalt him, and call upon his name.
text_cn: 友弟德说：“请你们向我的天主击鼓奏乐，向我的上主敲钹歌唱，向他吟咏诗歌，赞扬欢呼他的圣名！

text_en: For the Lord is a God who crushes wars; he sets up his camp among his people; he delivered me from the hands of my pursuers.
text_cn: 上主原是粉碎战争的天主，在民间支搭他的幕府，救我脱离仇人的毒手。

text_en: The Assyrian came down from the mountains of the north; he came with myriads of his warriors; their numbers blocked up the wadis, and their cavalry covered the hills.
text_cn: 亚述由北岳出发，率领着千军万马；大军阻塞了溪流，铁骑掩蔽了山丘。

text_en: He boasted that he would burn up my territory, and kill my young men with the sword, and dash my infants to the ground, and seize my children as booty, and take my virgins as spoil.
text_cn: 本想焚毁我村落，刀斩我青年，摔死我乳儿，俘掳我幼童，掠夺我妇女；

text_en: But the Lord Almighty has foiled them by the hand of a woman.
text_cn: 但全能上主，只凭一弱妇之手，把他们消除！

text_en: For their mighty one did not fall by the hands of the young men, nor did the sons of the Titans strike him down, nor did tall giants set upon him; but Judith daughter of Merari with the beauty of her countenance undid him.
text_cn: 亚述的名将，非壮丁所能击毙，非巨人之后所能击倒，非大力士所能征服，却为默辣黎之后友弟德，以她花容玉貌，使其心醉。

text_en: For she put away her widow’s clothing to exalt the oppressed in Israel. She anointed her face with perfume;
text_cn: 她脱去寡妇的衣服，去拯救受苦的以色列。香膏敷面，

text_en: she fastened her hair with a tiara and put on a linen gown to beguile him.
text_cn: 带束云髻，身披锦衣，为将他勾引。

text_en: Her sandal ravished his eyes, her beauty captivated his mind, and the sword severed his neck!
text_cn: 凉鞋夺目，玉容勾魂，短剑断其头。

text_en: The Persians trembled at her boldness, the Medes were daunted at her daring.
text_cn: 她的胆量，波斯人见而战栗；她的奋勇，玛待人因而恐惧。

text_en: Then my oppressed people shouted; my weak people cried out, and the enemy trembled; they lifted up their voices, and the enemy were turned back.
text_cn: 我卑微者一呼喊，他们便胆破；我弱小者一呐喊，他们便恐慌。 高声一嚷，他们都逃亡！

text_en: Sons of slave-girls pierced them through and wounded them like the children of fugitives; they perished before the army of my Lord.
text_cn: 少妇之子，将他们刺死，击杀他们像逃阵的小卒；我上主一布阵，他们即告灭亡。

text_en: I will sing to my God a new song: O Lord, you are great and glorious, wonderful in strength, invincible.
text_cn: 我要向我天主咏唱新歌： 上主，你伟大而荣耀，德能神妙，战无不胜！

text_en: Let all your creatures serve you, for you spoke, and they were made. You sent forth your spirit, and it formed them; there is none that can resist your voice.
text_cn: 愿你所造万物，都服侍你，因你一命，万物造成，你一嘘气，化工成形；你一发命，无人敢违。

text_en: For the mountains shall be shaken to their foundations with the waters; before your glance the rocks shall melt like wax. But to those who fear you you show mercy.
text_cn: 山岳振撼，山基随水而动，在你面前，磐石似蜡消溶； 但敬畏你的，你必仁慈怜悯。

text_en: For every sacrifice as a fragrant offering is a small thing, and the fat of all whole burnt offerings to you is a very little thing; but whoever fears the Lord is great forever.
text_cn: 祭祀原属小道，不过香烟一缕；种种燔祭油脂，于你实微不足道；但敬畏上主的人，伟大永存。

text_en: Woe to the nations that rise up against my people! The Lord Almighty will take vengeance on them in the day of judgment; he will send fire and worms into their flesh; they shall weep in pain forever.
text_cn: 祸哉，那攻击我族的异民！全能的上主在审判之日，必要报复，他们的肉体必受火烧虫蚀；哀痛哭泣，永不止息！”

text_en: When they arrived at Jerusalem, they worshiped God. As soon as the people were purified, they offered their burnt offerings, their freewill offerings, and their gifts.
text_cn: 百姓进入耶路撒冷，朝拜了天主；取洁之后， 奉献了全燔祭、自愿祭和供物。

text_en: Judith also dedicated to God all the possessions of Holofernes, which the people had given her; and the canopy that she had taken for herself from his bedchamber she gave as a votive offering.
text_cn: 友弟德将人民送给她的敖罗斐乃的各种物品，和拿自他寝室内的帷帐， 都献给了天主，作为还愿的献礼。

text_en: For three months the people continued feasting in Jerusalem before the sanctuary, and Judith remained with them.
text_cn: 三月之久，民众于耶路撒冷，在圣所前举行庆祝；友弟德也与他们同乐。

text_en: After this they all returned home to their own inheritances. Judith went to Bethulia, and remained on her estate. For the rest of her life she was honored throughout the whole country.
text_cn: 过了这个日期，各回本家，友弟德也回了拜突里雅，住在家里，一生到处受尊荣。

text_en: Many desired to marry her, but she gave herself to no man all the days of her life after her husband Manasseh died and was gathered to his people.
text_cn: 想念她的人，虽然很多，但她自从丈夫默纳舍去世，归于亲族之后，她一生岁月，再没有认识男人。

text_en: She became more and more famous, and grew old in her husband’s house, reaching the age of one hundred five. She set her maid free. She died in Bethulia, and they buried her in the cave of her husband Manasseh;
text_cn: 她活了很大的年纪，在他丈夫的家里，活到一百零五岁，解放了自己的奴婢，然后死在拜突里雅，埋葬在丈夫默纳舍的坟墓里。

text_en: and the house of Israel mourned her for seven days. Before she died she distributed her property to all those who were next of kin to her husband Manasseh, and to her own nearest kindred.
text_cn: 以色列家，举丧七天哀悼她。 她去世以前把家产分给了自己丈夫默纳舍的至亲，和自己的至亲家人。

text_en: No one ever again spread terror among the Israelites during the lifetime of Judith, or for a long time after her death.
text_cn: 友弟德在世之时，以及在她去世之后，很长久的时期，没有人敢扰乱以色列子民。
